newsitem.title: USA: M.G. Products loses Home Depot business.
newsitem.headline: M.G. Products loses Home Depot business.

text.p: M.G. Products Inc said Home Depot Inc, its largest customer, is terminating its orders for M.G. products under an ongoing sales program because the product shipments were delayed too often.
The company in a statement said the loss of Home Depot's business will further reduce 1997 sales revenue and may prevent the company from returning to profitability.
Eric Williams, M.G. Products, chief financial officer, told Reuters, "We've been changing our company, but not enough, and that has left us in a cash squeeze."
M.G. Products said Home Depot indicated it will make several purchases of existing inventory in the third quarter.

In a statement, M.G. Products, a lighting fixture maker, said it intends to signficantly restructure the operations of its corporate headquarters in San Antonio, Texas, and has begun to close down its production facility in Monterrey, Mexico. The facility is expected to be closed within 30 days; however, all open production orders will be filled.
The company said the cost containment efforts include laying off staff and streamlining day-to-day operations.
Morgan Guaranty Trust extended the maturity of a $2 million working capital loan from one to three years, the company said.
